title: Made It Their Own
theme: The R&B tradition of taking a song and making it more definitive than the original. From Dolly Parton to Whitney Houston. From Roberta Flack to The Fugees. From Stevie Wonder to Jodeci. The cover that becomes the version everyone remembers.
narrativePurpose: Test knowledge of the R&B and soul catalog of covers and remakes — the original recordings, the artists who transformed them, and the behind-the-scenes stories that explain how one version eclipses another.
toneProgression: The iconic covers everyone knows → the originals, albums, and producers behind the recordings → the archival stories that reveal why certain covers happened and what they cost

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-9-4 — the year Jodeci's 'Lately,' Mary J. Blige's 'I'm Goin' Down,' and Aaliyah's 'At Your Best (You Are Love)' were all released — three of the decade's most beloved R&B covers emerging in the same twelve months. 1994: the year R&B proved the original doesn't always have the last word.

rounds.description: The iconic covers everyone knows — and the originals they surpassed.

questions.question: Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You' — one of the best-selling singles of all time — was originally written and recorded by which country legend?

metadata.fact: Dolly Parton wrote and recorded 'I Will Always Love You' in 1973 as a farewell to her mentor Porter Wagoner. Whitney Houston's 1992 version for The Bodyguard became the best-selling single by a female artist.
metadata.storyHook: Dolly Parton wrote a goodbye. Whitney Houston turned it into one of the most powerful vocal performances in recording history.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Dolly Parton wrote and originally recorded 'I Will Always Love You.' Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Will_Always_Love_You

sources.title: I Will Always Love You – Wikipedia

questions.question: The Fugees' landmark cover of 'Killing Me Softly With His Song' (1996) appeared on which album?

metadata.song: Killing Me Softly With His Song
metadata.fact: 'Killing Me Softly' was the lead single from The Fugees' second and final studio album The Score (1996) — one of the best-selling rap albums of all time.
metadata.storyHook: The Fugees took Roberta Flack's 1973 recording and made it into something entirely their own. The Score did the same for hip-hop.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Killing Me Softly' appeared on The Fugees' album The Score. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Score_(album)

questions.question: Jodeci's 1993 smash 'Lately' — one of the most celebrated R&B covers of the decade — was originally written and recorded by which artist in 1980?

metadata.fact: 'Lately' was written and originally recorded by Stevie Wonder for his 1980 album Hotter Than July. Jodeci's 1993 cover became one of the era's signature performances.
metadata.storyHook: Stevie Wonder wrote it in 1980. Jodeci made an entirely new generation feel it.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Lately' was written and recorded by Stevie Wonder on Hotter Than July (1980). Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lately_(Stevie_Wonder_song)

questions.question: Dolly Parton wrote 'I Will Always Love You' as a personal farewell to which Grand Ole Opry star — her mentor and TV show host — when she decided to leave his variety program?

metadata.fact: Dolly Parton wrote 'I Will Always Love You' as her 'goodbye song to Porter' — a farewell to Porter Wagoner when she decided to leave his syndicated TV show and pursue a solo career.
metadata.storyHook: It wasn't a love song. It was a resignation letter. Dolly Parton wrote one of the most beautiful goodbyes in music history to her boss.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Dolly Parton wrote 'I Will Always Love You' as a farewell to Porter Wagoner. Source: Parade https://parade.com/news/dolly-parton-heartbreaking-goodbye-man-never-stopped-loving-porter-wagoner-i-will-always-love-you

sources.title: Dolly Parton's Heartbreaking Goodbye to Porter Wagoner – Parade

questions.question: 'Killing Me Softly With His Song' was not written by Roberta Flack. The song was inspired by a concert that songwriter Lori Lieberman attended — specifically moved by the performance of which folk artist?

metadata.artist: Lori Lieberman / Roberta Flack / The Fugees
metadata.song: Killing Me Softly With His Song
metadata.fact: Lori Lieberman wrote the original version in 1971 after attending a Don McLean concert at The Troubadour and being deeply moved by his performance of 'Empty Chairs.' Norman Gimbel and Charles Fox then set her poem to music.
metadata.storyHook: Don McLean performed at The Troubadour. Lori Lieberman walked out and wrote a poem. That poem became one of the most covered songs in R&B history.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Killing Me Softly' was inspired by Lori Lieberman's emotional response to a Don McLean concert, specifically 'Empty Chairs.' Sources: The Daily Hatch https://thedailyhatch.org/2023/08/10/lori-lieberman-wrote-killing-me-softly-after-attending-a-don-mclean-concert-in-1970-during-, YouTube https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hPRswF993Xo

sources.title: Lori Lieberman wrote 'Killing Me Softly' after attending a Don McLean concert – The Daily Hatch

questions.question: Elvis Presley wanted to record 'I Will Always Love You' — but the deal collapsed because his manager demanded 50% of the song's publishing rights, which Dolly Parton refused to surrender. Who was that manager?

metadata.fact: Colonel Tom Parker's standard demand for 50% of publishing rights blocked Elvis from recording 'I Will Always Love You.' Dolly Parton refused. She has said she's glad the deal fell through — and has described the moment she heard Whitney Houston's version.
metadata.storyHook: Colonel Tom Parker wanted half. Dolly Parton said no. Elvis never recorded the song. Then Whitney Houston did.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Colonel Tom Parker blocked Elvis from recording 'I Will Always Love You' by demanding 50% of publishing rights. Sources: Whiskey Riff https://www.whiskeyriff.com/2023/11/17/colonel-tom-parker-stopped-elvis-from-recording-i-will-always-love-you-because-dolly-refu, Facebook https://www.facebook.com/EricAlperPR/posts/when-colonel-tom-parker-wanted-elvis-presley-to-record-dolly-partons-i-will-alwa/1522

sources.title: Colonel Tom Parker Stopped Elvis From Recording 'I Will Always Love You'
When Colonel Tom Parker wanted Elvis Presley to record 'I Will Always Love You' – Eric Alper post

questions.question: Roberta Flack's 1973 recording of 'Killing Me Softly With His Song' is widely treated as the original — but the song was first recorded in 1972 by which singer-songwriter who had written the poem that inspired it?

metadata.song: Killing Me Softly With His Song
metadata.fact: Lori Lieberman's recording of 'Killing Me Softly With His Song' was released in 1972 (recorded late 1971) — a year before Roberta Flack's version made it famous. Lieberman wrote the poem that became the song's lyrics after attending a Don McLean concert.
metadata.storyHook: Everyone knows Roberta Flack's version. Everyone knows The Fugees' version. Almost nobody knows Lori Lieberman's name — even though she got there first.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Lori Lieberman's original recording was released in 1972, recorded late 1971. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_Me_Softly_with_His_Song, Yahoo article https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/lori-lieberman-first-sang-killing-201524923.html

sources.title: Killing Me Softly with His Song – Wikipedia
Lori Lieberman, Who First Sang 'Killing Me Softly with His Song' – Yahoo article
